raw_response:
*sits down on a low stool, lights a cigarette, thinks*

I'm 54 now, been working this land about thirty years. 8 mu isn't much, but with the wife and me, and the kids who come back to help when they can, we manage. Two of our sons work in town — one in Handan, one in a factory down south — and they send some money home, which is good because otherwise 8 mu doesn't feed seven mouths.

Of the 8 mu, about 5 mu I do wheat-then-maize, same as most families around here. The other 3 mu I keep in cotton. That piece of land near the ditch is a little salty, cotton doesn't mind it as much as grain does. And cotton gives us cash — the grain mostly we eat or feed, but the cotton we sell.

### The wheat (5 mu) — already in the ground

Put it in last October, around the 10th. I always plant around then, same as my father did. Used the regular variety from the agro-store, about 15 kg seed per mu, saved some of my own too.

Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kg bag. That's what everybody does. It's coming out of winter now and the color looks OK, not too yellow. When it hits jointing, maybe late April, I'll topdress half a bag of urea per mu. If the wheat looks weak I'll put more, but one bag compound plus half a bag urea is my normal.

Winter water already went in before the freeze. I'll irrigate once at jointing and once when the grain is filling. Three times total. The well is close but the electricity meter runs — I don't pump more than I need.

Last year I got about 420 kg per mu off the wheat. If the weather cooperates I expect about the same.

### The maize (5 mu) — follows wheat in June

The day the combine comes through for the wheat, I'm already thinking about maize. You can't wait — every day you lose is yield gone. I don't do real tillage, just call Old Wang with the no-till planter, he charges about 30 yuan per mu and it's done in half a day.

Seed I buy fresh every year — hybrid seed from the agro-store, whatever they're pushing. Around 40 yuan per mu. Same fertilizer routine: one bag compound at planting, half a bag urea when it's about knee-high, around the big-bell stage. Put the urea right next to the row.

Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat. If July is dry I'll irrigate once around tasseling. If there's rain I don't. Usually spray herbicide once when it's small and maybe one spray for armyworm if I see them. Last year maize came in around 480 kg per mu.

### The cotton (3 mu) — the one that takes real work

Plant mid-April, when the soil has warmed enough. I use Bt cotton seed from the store — used to be bollworm would eat everything but these new seeds handle it better. Still I spray maybe three or four times through the summer for bollworm, aphids, what have you.

Cotton I don't fertilize as heavy as grain. Half a bag of compound before planting, then maybe 15-20 kg of urea later when it starts putting on squares. Any more and it grows too many leaves and not enough bolls — my father-in-law taught me that.

Irrigation maybe twice — once for establishment if April-May is dry, once in the bloom period. Then the real work is summer: every few days walking the rows, pulling side branches, hoeing weeds, picking when the bolls open. My wife and I do all the picking, that goes September through October, three or four passes. Last year about 250 kg seed cotton per mu.

### What I'm watching

Main worry is the rain. If May stays dry I'll have to pump more for cotton establishment, and that's extra money. Fertilizer prices also went up this winter — I heard from the shop owner in town. If prices keep climbing I might skip the second urea topdress on maize, see if I can get away with less. But I'm not changing the wheat — that's our flour for the year, I won't skimp.
